findings.claim: ICDAR 2023 IHTR: IIIT-INDIC-HW dataset, 10 scripts (bn/hi/gu/pa/kn/ml/or/ta/te/ur), ~700K-850K train images per script; winner Upstage KR 95.94% char accuracy.

IHTR-2023 detail: 18 teams registered, 6 submitted; Upstage KR avg CRR 95.94 and WRR 88.31 across 10 scripts. Per-script tables are in the paper, NOT in the ledger (Bengali 96.10 WRR in plan not verifiable here).

CONTRADICTION: plan says IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS is CC-BY-4.0; ledger says IHTR dataset card + IHDR dataset card released under ACADEMIC-USE license, and D4 bars training on these for W6 unless on SAFE langs.
IHTR dataset card: IIIT-INDIC-HW allows additional training data; released under academic-use license (licence claim, re-check against plan's CC-BY-4.0).

IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS (Gongidi & Jawahar ICDAR 2021): 868K handwritten word instances, 135 writers, 8 scripts listed (list names 9) + IIIT-HW-DEV + IIIT-HW-TELUGU = 10 scripts. Best in-domain CER 9.64% (10K pretrain), 4.97% (82K).
IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS ablation: IAM English handwriting pretraining helps slightly (4.85% CER vs 4.97%): small positive cross-script transfer supports shared backbone + per-script head.
Ledger inference: 2021 baseline ~5% CER on clean HW words means bottleneck is handwriting x scan x rare-script, not clean handwriting recognition.

SemiHastakshar (IIIT-H, Dec 2025): semi-supervised Indic HTR trained on IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS (labeled) + IIIT-INDIC-HW-WILD (new, unlabeled, internet) + IIIT-Indic-HW-UC (unlabeled); compared vs PARSeq HTR baseline; closes generalisation gap. Relevant to HW2 independent-writers gate.
ICDAR 2025 IHDR: page-level Indic handwriting across 13 scripts; allowed pretraining sets IIIT-Indic-HW-UC (13 langs), IHWWR-1.0, PLHWTR-1.0, IHTR-2023, IHTR-2022; winner 2025-05-15.
PLATTER (arXiv 2502.06172, IIIT-H): page-level transformer HTR for Indic, open-source, competed in IHDR-2025; candidate page-level handwriting base.
IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS mirrors: HF c3rl Hindi-only subset; IndiaAI Kosh mirror lists 13 langs vs original 10 (extension over time); IIIT-HW-Dev 1.8GB, IIIT-HW-Telugu 3.7GB.
ICDAR 2025 HNU challenge: 2,000 handwritten science note pages + 1,000 QA pairs; 16 teams, 6 valid; even SOTA VLMs fail badly on handwritten reasoning.
Sarvam Vision 2.1 launch (2026-09-24/25) claims Indic handwriting recognition; Bodhan IndicOCR (0.8B, 15M+ docs, live 2026-09-05) explicitly targets handwriting and old newspapers.
Bhashini ULCA OCR catalog: IIITH-OCR-SceneText for 8 langs (as/bn/gu/hi/kn/ml/mni/mr) - production baseline for scene-text, not HW.

Sarvam Vision 2.1 Indic OCR Bench: overall 87.39; Bodhan 84.94; Gemini 3.6 Flash 79.35; Google Cloud Vision 71.76. No Wilson CI/McNemar/abstention. Bench 6,909 samples (6,609 Indic + 300 EN), 22 langs + EN.

Sarvam 2.1 per-language word accuracy: Santali 53.91 (weakest), Kashmiri 54.82, Manipuri 85.12, Odia 80.01, Maithili 96.70, Konkani 97.41, Nepali 97.00, Marathi 95.06, Hindi 95.91, Bengali 92.61, Tamil 93.42, Telugu 87.70. Only public per-script table.
Chandra OCR 2 olmOCR subsets: Old Scans 51.1, Old Scans Math 89.1, Tables 92.1, Multi column 82.1, ArXiv 86.9; overall 85.8 (adjusted from 85.9). Compare Sarvam OldScan 55.3.
olmOCR-Bench OldScan subset (442 pages): Surya 2 42.8, olmOCR-2 82.2, GPT-5.x ~85, Claude ~85; 40+ point range shows OldScan universally hard; Sarvam OldScan 55.3 is mid-pack.

LightOnOCR-2-1B (Apache-2.0, 1B): olmOCR Old Scans 84.7, Math 76.1, Tables 78.6, Long Tiny Text 81.2 - an open 1B model scoring far above Chandra 2's 51.1 on Old Scans (different table versions; unclear comparability).

Printed low-resource baseline (Sarkar et al IIIT-H, Mozhi-LR(S), CRNN+LM): word accuracy Kashmiri 93.80, Ol Chiki Santali 96.58, Bodo 97.22, Nepali 95.13 - a small specialist reaches 93-97 where Sarvam VLM gets 53.91/54.82 (different data).
Indic-OCR Project (indic-ocr.github.io): open Tesseract models incl. Ol Chiki and Meetei Mayek, 'perhaps the best set of Tesseract models for Indic'. Fallback path for sat/mni.
ScriptMoE (shared encoder + top-2 script experts + shared expert): PP-OCRv5 F1 65.71 to 80.89, scene text; Ol Chiki and Meitei Mayek NOT among its 10 scripts.
Ledger probe22 sees ks as Perso-Arabic/Nastaliq cousin; KITAB-Bench (Arabic, 8,809 samples, 36 sub-domains, CC-BY-4.0) could give a second-source Nastaliq signal for ks routing.

Warp is the weakest Real5-OmniDocBench distortion (PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 91.25) vs scan 94.74 (strongest); overall 93.19; 1,355 pages x5 classes = 6,775 renderings. Suggests curvature not scan is bottleneck for OldScan restoration (R4).

Restoration toolbox cited: DocRes (5 tasks, DTSPrompt), Uni-DocDiff, TextSR (OCR-guided diffusion SR), UniT, DocRevive (30,078 synthetic degraded images), D2Dewarp, cubic-polynomial dewarp (median CER 0.0235 IWILT), binarization fair-eval (SauvolaNet + DE-GAN lead on DIBCO 2017).

Scrambled-text synthetic corruption post-correction (Bourne, IJDAR 2025): median CER -55%, WER -32% over base Llama on Hindi OCR error correction; beats real-data training; low corruption levels needed. Supports synthetic post-correction.
MinerU2.5-Pro: 1.2B (NaViT-675M + Qwen2-0.5B), 95.69 OmniDocBench v1.6 (+2.71 vs 92.98) via data engineering; 65.5M samples; 3-stage (pretrain, hard-sample FT, GRPO). 1.2B beats 235B general VLM.
MonkeyOCR: weights research/non-commercial only (code Apache-2.0); v2 1.2B beats 3B by 7.4% on Chinese via CPD; 3B runs on single RTX 3090 0.84 pg/s. DIES for commercial ship.

DeepSeek-OCR: MIT, 6.68GB, 3B MoE (570M active), 380M DeepEncoder, 97% on Fox at 10x compression, 200K pages/day single A100; trained 70% OCR / 20% general vision / 10% text; catastrophic repetition up to 71x ref length on Hindi.

PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (0.9B, Apache-2.0): 96.33 OmniDocBench v1.6; ~2GB VRAM FP16, ~45 pg/min on L40S; GLM-OCR 0.9B 1.86 pg/s; Surya 2 0.65B 5.35 pg/s on RTX5090; surya license modified OpenRAIL-M weights (free <$5M).
Chitrapathak-2 (Krutrim): 9 Indian govt doc types, 89.8% exact match, ~1.03 s/doc vLLM; Tesseract+LLM only 21.22% EM; fine-tuned Nanonets-OCR2-3B (Qwen2.5-VL); 10 langs + EN.
Sarvam doc-digitise API Rs0.5/page: 5,344 pages = Rs2,672 (~$32), Jun-2026 67% cut; full run needs explicit user approval per D1; paid key, so DIES as pipeline component.
Surya v0.22.1 breaking change: layout/OCR/table-rec now need an inference backend (Docker+NVIDIA GPU or llama...) - hurts portability/offline CPU claims.

PyTorch/MLX portability point: Chandra 2 OpenRAIL-M free only under $2M revenue; MinerU Apache-2.0 + commercial threshold (>1B MAU or >$20M monthly rev) and attribution; licence audit needed before shipping.

Devanagari stress test (Singh 2026): synthetic chrF++ 91-98 hides all differences; on 300 real Hindi scans 9/10 systems collapse; English OCR rank does not transfer (GPT-5.5 58.5, olmOCR-7B 40.5, Qwen3-VL-8B 75.2, Opus 4.7 82.2, Gemini 2.5 Flash 86.3).

Catastrophic-failure taxonomy: surface (numerals/punct), structural (conjunct/matra/nukta), hallucination (repetition; DeepSeek 71x length). Report median + catastrophic rate, not mean CER. Probe22 raw-vs-normalised delta 0.6707 vs 0.6692 (0.0015) shows errors are structural.

Eval discipline law (section 9): Wilson 95% CI per cell, McNemar exact paired on same items, abstention-coverage column, per-row uncapped CER, cer_100_count, empty pred = CER 1.0; evalci library for Wilson+McNemar. OmniDocBench lacks abstention/CI.
Wilson CI backed by NIST dataplot, Wallis 2022 (Newcombe-Wilson paired), Fagerland 2014 (McNemar mid-p); evalci (arXiv 2607.04429) implements them. Std-dev across >=3 runs recommended.

Sarvam Indic OCR Bench cannot be downloaded without user approval (section 9 hard rule); A4-031 is an UNKNOWN placeholder; internal probe22 (n=1227, 18 langs, ~100/lang) is the primary eval until approved. Research license: Sarvam research-use.
FaithC4 (Amazon): general VLMs rewrite imperfect text (WER +6.9), OCR-specialized VLMs stay faithful (+0.1-3.4); relevant to post-correction hallucination risk.
CER buckets: good 1-2%, average 2-10%, poor >10%. Reul 2021 survey: CER=(i+s+d)/n; report CER+WER+confidence metric; NIST IR4990 error-vs-rejection curves = modern abstention-coverage.

Sarvam Vision v1 (Feb 2026, 3B state-space VLM): Hindi 95.91, Bengali 92.61, Tamil 93.42, Telugu 87.70 on Indic OCR Bench; ArXiv Math 86.5 vs Mistral OCR 3 85.4; v2.1 87.3 olmOCR / 87.39 Indic, ranked 2nd to PaddleOCR on structure preservation.

Competitor landscape: Mistral OCR 3 $2/1000 pages ($1 batch), 74% win vs v2 on forms/handwriting; Sarvam funding $75M Series B valuation $1.43B (total $350M); LEAP Hackathon PS-2 winner Multilipi, runner-up Soochna Sahayak (Bhashini).
Bodhan AI (IITM CoE) is a sovereign education DPI; classroom worksheet digitisation is the demo angle; Bodhan IndicOCR 0.8B open weights, sibling Indic-Transcribe 1B ASR.

Whole-benchmark transferability: OmniDocBench (1,355 pages, 9 types incl. handwritten notes) not Indic; Sarvam/Bodhan not on board; KITAB-style multi-level GT proposed as template for an Indic OCR Bench v2.

Ledger design pattern: 2-stage layout+recognition (PaddleOCR-VL, MinerU2.5, MonkeyOCR SRR, DocLayoutYOLO) is the proven pattern; plan's Page Expert (IndicDocLayout 33M + IndicBlockOCR 0.8B) matches. IndicDLP (AI4Bharat, Jun 2026) is the layout-tier benchmark.

olmOCR-bench leaderboard (Surya README): Infinity-Parser2-Pro 35.1B 87.6; Chandra OCR 2 4.0B 85.9; dots.mocr 3.0B 83.9; Surya OCR 2 0.65B 83.3; LightOnOCR 2-1B 83.2; Chandra 1 9.0B 83.1; olmOCR 8.3B 77.4; GOT OCR 0.6B 48.3.
Chitrapathak-2 IndicVisionBench ANLS: Telugu char-ANLS 6.69 vs 11.00 for v1 (envelope only).
Script router base candidates: ICDAR MLT-2019 cropped-word script-ID (10-way, Hindi+Bangla only), BSTD (12 langs, 6,582 images, 126,292 words, Apache-2.0, PARSeq+DBNet) and IndicPhotoOCR toolkit.

BSTD/IndicPhotoOCR: PARSeq recognizer trained on synthetic data then fine-tuned = 2025 SOTA for Indic scene text; IndicPhotoOCR hosts PARSeq + DBNet pretrained for 12 langs (corroborates plan's local checkpoints).

BHASHA 2025: 14 SOTA OCR models evaluated on Indic scripts, big CER reduction from fine-tuning on ancient handwriting data; GCN-verifier (ResNet-50+GCN) on Hindi books as post-corrector candidate; SimPO as DPO alternative for Stage-3b.
MinerU2.5-Pro GRPO Stage 3b recipe marked adopt in ledger; W6 constraints: no paid keys, no training until W6 freeze, open weights + local QLoRA only, 200-dpi citizen docs.

Ledger ends with unresolved UNKNOWN/REJECTED records: AIR-Bench (A4-047 REJECTED, IR not OCR), akshara-level CER Bhat (A4-085 UNKNOWN), A4-055 UNKNOWN failed verify; sat/ks/mni rows measured only via probe22.
Mixing rule: synthetic + real required; CMTLAB (ICDAR 2019 MLT, E2E F1 71.13) beat pure-real via synthetic; synthetic alone caps CER, real data needed for last 5-15 points.

plan_v4_gaps: Plan cites IIIT-INDIC-HW-WORDS as CC-BY-4.0 but ledger shows academic-use license on IHTR/IHDR dataset cards and a D4 rule barring training on them except SAFE langs (LEDGER.md:6137, 6121). Verify license before HW2.

Plan has no semi-supervised/unlabeled-real step; SemiHastakshar uses IIIT-INDIC-HW-WILD + HW-UC unlabeled to close writer generalisation gap vs PARSeq baseline (LEDGER.md:6153) - relevant to HW2 >=85% independent writers.
Plan lacks eval discipline: Wilson 95% CI, McNemar exact, catastrophic-rate (pred_len > 5x ref), abstention-coverage column, median CER (LEDGER.md:6643, 6960, 6635).
Plan relies on handwriting-tier numbers but ledger shows English/synthetic benchmarks do not transfer to Indic real scans (chrF++ 91-98 synthetic vs 9/10 collapse) (LEDGER.md:6463, 6886).

Plan's Bodhan/Sarvam comparators come from Sarvam's own bench: Bodhan 84.94 vs Sarvam 87.39 vs Gemini 79.35 vs GCV 71.76, no CI (LEDGER.md:6233); cannot be reproduced without user-approved download (LEDGER.md:6205).

Weak cells sat 53.91 / ks 54.82 / mni 85.12 / or 80.01 and OldScan 55.3 not addressed in HW-only plan; ledger has Tesseract Ol Chiki/Mayek models and 93-97% printed specialist baselines (LEDGER.md:5046, 5054, 6225).
Restoration (R4) options absent: DocRes, TextSR, dewarping; warp is weakest distortion (91.25) (LEDGER.md:6027, 5190).
Surya 2 now needs an inference backend (Docker/GPU), conflicting with portable offline claim; Chandra 2 OpenRAIL-M $2M limit; MonkeyOCR weights non-commercial (LEDGER.md:5594, 4910, 4734).
Page-level handwriting (PLATTER, IHDR-2025 13 scripts) and handwriting QA (HNU-2025) are tiers the plan ignores (LEDGER.md:6129, 6145, 6185).

Post-correction: scrambled-text synthetic corruption gives CER -55% on Hindi (LEDGER.md:5238), FaithC4 warns general VLMs rewrite text (LEDGER.md:5278), BHASHA GCN verifier option (LEDGER.md:6934); plan's post-correction lacks a faithfulness check.
